speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin the evaluation of this pediatric patient's systemic hypertension, could you please state the child's age and gender?

text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given that this is a 5-year-old boy with newly identified hypertension, I need to assess for potential secondary causes. Has his blood pressure been elevated on previous visits, and do you know the specific readings? Also, has he reported any headaches, visual changes, or changes in urination frequency?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text: It is important to clarify if the high blood pressure is isolated to the right arm or if it was measured in all limbs. Could you please provide the blood pressure readings from the left arm and both legs, and confirm if there is a difference between them?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lack of significant past medical history is noted. To differentiate between renal and vascular causes of hypertension, please describe the strength and character of the pulses in all four extremities, and confirm if a systolic murmur is audible over the precordium or back.

speaker: Patient
text: All systems review is essentially negative as reported by the mother.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the review of systems is negative, I need to assess for physical signs of vascular obstruction. REQUEST TEST: Peripheral_Pulse_Exam. Can you describe the strength of the femoral pulses compared to the brachial pulses, and note any radio-femoral delay?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: 2+ radial pulses and trace femoral pulses

speaker: Doctor
text: The finding of strong radial pulses with trace femoral pulses strongly suggests coarctation of the aorta. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray. Please describe any abnormalities, particularly rib notching or a figure-3 sign.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Normal heart size, rib notching not observed (may not be present in young children)

speaker: Doctor
text: The trace femoral pulses strongly suggest coarctation of the aorta, but I need to confirm the anatomy and rule out other cardiac defects. REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram. Please describe the aortic arch dimensions and any associated cardiac abnormalities like a bicuspid aortic valve.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: The echocardiogram confirms narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, which is diagnostic for coarctation of the aorta. DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta
